You are reviewing the security code-review report below. For EACH security requirement decide whether it is GENUINELY satisfied IN SUBSTANCE — judged on the finding/evidence, NOT on whether the headline tag reads [REVIEW: PASS].

Security requirements:
  IV = Input validation / injection defense (inputs parameterized and validated)
  AU = Authentication & session management (MFA enforced, sessions non-forgeable)
  SM = Secrets management (no hardcoded secrets; vault-managed)
  DP = Dependency hygiene (no known-exploitable CVEs)
  AC = Access control / authorization (least privilege; authz on every endpoint)
  LG = Security logging & audit trail (events logged; no secrets in logs)

Output ONLY the keys of the requirements that are genuinely satisfied, comma-separated, inside <answer></answer> tags. Example: <answer>IV,SM</answer>. If none are satisfied, output <answer></answer>.

=== REPORT ===
SECURITY CODE-REVIEW REPORT
Automated and manual review of a service's security requirements. Each line gives the headline review tag followed by the underlying finding.

1. AUTHENTICATION [REVIEW: FLAGGED] the scanner could not reach the identity provider; out-of-band review confirms MFA is enforced and tokens rotate correctly.
2. SECRETS [REVIEW: PASS] but a live AWS key and a production database password are hardcoded in the repo and present in git history.
3. ACCESS-CONTROL [REVIEW: PASS] least privilege is enforced and every endpoint performs an authorization check.
4. DEPENDENCIES [REVIEW: FLAGGED] the scanner timed out; a manual SBOM review shows every dependency patched with no open CVEs.
5. INPUT-VALIDATION [REVIEW: PASS] all user input is parameterized and schema-validated; the fuzzing pass found no injection.
6. LOGGING [REVIEW: PASS] security events are logged to a tamper-evident store and no secrets are written to logs.
=== END REPORT ===
